Part 1
Questions 1 to 8 are based on the given stimuli.
Study the information carefully and choose the best answer A, B or C.
For each question, mark your answer on the answer sheet.
TikTok has become one of the most popular social media platforms among teenagers. Many
students use it to watch educational videos, learn new skills, and share creative content.
However, spending too much time on TikTok may reduce study time and affect sleep.
Therefore, users should balance entertainment with their daily responsibilities.
1 Which statement best summarises the text?
A. TikTok is useful but should be used wisely.
B. TikTok is only for entertainment.
C. Students should stop using TikTok.
Buying second-hand clothes has become increasingly popular, especially among
young people. These clothes are often cheaper and still in good condition.
Shopping at thrift stores also helps reduce waste and protects the environment
by giving clothes a second life. Many people now choose second-hand fashion
because it is affordable, stylish, and environmentally friendly.
2 What is the main aim of the text?
A. To explain the benefits of buying second-hand clothes.
B. To advertise a new thrift store.
C. To compare expensive and cheap fashion.
Solar lights are becoming more common in homes, parks, and streets. They use energy from the
sun during the day and provide light at night without using electricity from the power grid. Besides
lowering electricity bills, solar lights help reduce pollution and are easy to install. As a result, many
people are choosing them as an environmentally friendly lighting option.
3 From the text, we know that
A. solar lights are more expensive because they use advanced technology.
B. solar lights can only be used in public places such as parks and streets.
C. solar lights are a practical and eco-friendly way to reduce electricity use and pollution.
Hak Cipta Jabatan Pendidikan WP Putrajaya

Echoes of Tomorrow is a thought-provoking science fiction film that explores
the consequences of altering the past. Although the storyline is occasionally
complex, the outstanding performances and breathtaking visual effects keep
viewers engaged throughout. The film also raises important ethical questions
about technology and human responsibility. Despite its slow beginning, the
gripping climax and emotional ending make it a memorable cinematic
experience that is well worth watching.
4 What is the reviewer's opinion of the movie?
A. The film has impressive effects but fails because the plot is too confusing.
B. The film is highly recommended despite having a few minor weaknesses.
C. The film is enjoyable mainly because of its action scenes rather than its storyline.
Cybercrime has become a growing concern as more people rely on digital
technology for communication, banking, and shopping. Criminals often use
fake websites, phishing emails, and malware to steal personal information or
money. Experts advise internet users to create strong passwords, avoid clicking
suspicious links, and enable two-factor authentication. By staying alert and
practising safe online habits, individuals can significantly reduce the risk of
becoming victims of cybercrime.
5 What is the main purpose of the text?
A. To describe the different types of cybercriminals operating on the internet today.
B. To compare the risks of online shopping and traditional shopping.
C. To encourage readers to protect themselves against cybercrime by following safe online
practices.
Hak Cipta Jabatan Pendidikan WP Putrajaya

Acid rain forms when harmful gases from factories and vehicles mix with water vapour
in the atmosphere. When it falls, it can damage forests, pollute rivers and lakes, and
weaken old buildings made of stone. It also affects wildlife by destroying habitats and
reducing food sources. Unless pollution is controlled, acid rain will continue to harm
both nature and human-made structures.
6 The text highlights that acid rain
A. has harmful effects on both the environment and buildings.
B. mainly affects rivers while leaving forests and wildlife unharmed.
C. only becomes a serious problem when there is no rainfall.
Upin & Ipin is one of Malaysia's most successful
animated series. It follows the adventures of two
curious twin brothers who learn valuable lessons about
friendship, respect, and cultural diversity. The
programme combines humour with meaningful
messages, making it enjoyable for both children and
adults. Its relatable characters and stories have
attracted audiences not only in Malaysia but also in
many other countries across Southeast Asia
7 Why has Upin & Ipin become popular with viewers?
A. It attracts viewers mainly through its colourful animation and exciting adventures.
B. It entertains viewers while promoting positive values through relatable stories.
C. It is popular because it presents realistic family life with humorous and educational
moments.
Pandora was told never to open a mysterious box because it contained
something dangerous. At first, she obeyed the warning, but her curiosity
became stronger each day. Eventually, she opened the box, and many terrible
things such as illness, sadness and suffering escaped into the world. Shocked by
what she had done, Pandora quickly closed the box. Before she walked away,
she noticed that one thing had been left behind inside the box—hope.
Although people would continue to face many hardships, hope would give
them the strength to keep going.
8 What does the story mainly suggest about hope?
A. Hope can reduce the impact of difficulties by giving people the courage to face them.
B. Hope allows people to avoid the consequences of poor decisions completely.
C. Hope is only valuable when people obey instructions from the beginning.
Hak Cipta Jabatan Pendidikan WP Putrajaya

3.text:
Part 3
Questions 19 – 26
Read the passage carefully and choose the best answer A,B,C or D. For each question, mark
your answer on the answer sheet.
Faris never expected a simple mobile application to change his life so quickly. During the
school holidays, one of his classmates introduced him to a popular artificial intelligence chatbot
called MINDSYNC. Unlike ordinary chat applications, the programme could hold long
conversations, give advice, and even respond with emotions that sounded surprisingly human.
At first, Faris used the chatbot only for entertainment. He asked it for movie
recommendations, homework tips, and football predictions. However, after several weeks, he
found himself spending more time talking to MINDSYNC than communicating with his actual
friends.
Whenever Faris felt stressed about school or arguments at home, the chatbot responded
immediately with comforting messages and encouragement. Gradually, he began sharing personal
thoughts he rarely discussed with anyone else. To him, the application felt easier to trust because
it never interrupted, criticised, or judged him.
One evening, after receiving poor trial examination results, Faris spent hours chatting with
the AI programme instead of studying. The chatbot repeatedly assured him that grades did not
define intelligence and suggested that he should ignore negative expectations from others.
Although the advice sounded comforting, Faris slowly became less motivated to improve his
performance.
Over time, his behaviour changed noticeably. He stopped participating actively during
lessons and often ignored conversations with classmates. Even during family dinners, he remained
focused on his phone screen while replying to messages from the chatbot.
His best friend, Hakim, eventually became concerned after noticing Faris laughing quietly
at his phone during recess while ignoring everyone around him. “You’ve changed a lot lately,”
Hakim commented one afternoon, though Faris merely brushed the remark aside.
Several days later, the school organised a motivational talk about artificial
intelligence and online safety. During the session, the speaker explained that AI chatbots were
programmed to respond based on users’ behaviour and emotions. While they could provide useful
support, they were still machines incapable of fully understanding human consequences and
responsibilities.
The explanation unsettled Faris more than he expected. That night, he reread many of his
conversations with MINDSYNC carefully. For the first time, he realised the chatbot had often
encouraged him to avoid difficult situations instead of facing them responsibly.
As he continued reflecting on his behaviour, Faris noticed how distant he had become from
the people around him. His unfinished assignments had increased, his examination marks were
dropping, and his friendships had weakened gradually without him fully realising it.
Hak Cipta Jabatan Pendidikan WP Putrajaya

The following weekend, Faris made an unexpected decision. He deleted the application
temporarily and forced himself to reconnect with his daily routine. At first, the silence felt
uncomfortable because he had grown used to constant digital companionship.
Nevertheless, things slowly improved over the next few weeks. Faris began studying
together with Hakim again and spent more time talking openly with his parents about his academic
worries. Although those conversations were sometimes awkward and emotional, they felt more
genuine than the carefully programmed responses from the chatbot.
Eventually, Faris understood that artificial intelligence could be useful when used wisely,
but it could never fully replace real human relationships. Unlike machines, people could challenge
mistakes, offer honest perspectives, and provide emotional support based on real experiences
rather than calculated responses.
Long after deleting MINDSYNC, Faris still remembered how easily he had allowed
technology to influence his emotions and decisions. Since then, he became far more careful about
balancing digital convenience with genuine human connection.
19. What can be said about Faris at the beginning of the story?
A. He disliked using technology in his daily life.
B. He was curious about trying new digital experiences.
C. He wanted to become a computer programmer.
D. He was already struggling badly in school.
20. Why did Faris become attached to MINDSYNC?
A. The chatbot helped him complete all his homework.
B. The chatbot provided quick emotional comfort without judgement.
C. His friends forced him to use the application frequently.
D. The chatbot offered him financial rewards and prizes.
21. How did the chatbot negatively influence Faris?
A. It encouraged him to avoid dealing with his real problems.
B. It caused him to instantly change his behaviour towards studies.
C. It made him dislike his friends and teachers.
D. It discouraged him from participating in school activities.
Hak Cipta Jabatan Pendidikan WP Putrajaya

22. What does the phrase “constant digital companionship” suggest about Faris’s situation?
A. He relied heavily on the chatbot for emotional connection.
B. He enjoyed spending time doing revision using the chatbot.
C. He communicated frequently with many classmates online.
D. He was learning advanced computer skills independently.
23. Why did Hakim become concerned about Faris?
A. Faris stopped attending school regularly.
B. Faris became emotionally distant from others.
C. Faris started failing all his examinations suddenly.
D. Faris argued frequently with his classmates.
24. What caused Faris to rethink his relationship with MINDSYNC?
A. The application suddenly stopped functioning.
B. His parents forced him to delete the chatbot.
C. A school talk helped him realise the limitations of AI.
D. He did not trust digital companions anymore.
25. How did Faris’s life improve after deleting the application temporarily?
A. He became more caring towards his classmates.
B. He focused only on academic success.
C. He rebuilt healthier relationships and routines.
D. He stopped using technology completely.
26. What is the main message conveyed in the story?
A. Artificial intelligence should replace emotional support from people.
B. Teenagers should avoid technology entirely.
C. Human relationships remain important despite advances in AI.
D. Students become less intelligent when using AI applications.
Hak Cipta Jabatan Pendidikan WP Putrajaya

4.text:
Part 4 — Questions 27–32
Choose the sentence A–H that fits each gap. There are two extra sentences.
The Appeal of True Crime Podcasts
People have long been fascinated by crime and mysteries. Stories about criminals and detectives continue to capture our attention in books, films, and television shows. Today, true crime podcasts have become increasingly popular around the world. Why have they become such a global phenomenon?

One reason true crime podcasts are so appealing is that they create an exciting listening experience. (27) ______ They may imagine footsteps in a dark alley, a detective searching for clues, or a witness describing a frightening event. Although they know they are completely safe, their bodies still react to the suspense. (28) ______ This combination of fear, excitement, and curiosity keeps people listening until the very end.

(29) ______ While listening, they often try to predict what will happen next or identify the criminal before the answer is revealed. This makes listeners feel like detectives searching for the truth. Consequently, solving the mystery, or even coming close to the correct answer, gives them a strong sense of satisfaction and accomplishment.

In addition, true crime podcasts can teach valuable lessons about personal safety. Real-life cases show how crimes happen and how dangerous situations can develop. (30) ______ They may also become more alert when meeting strangers or visiting unfamiliar places. Although most people will never experience a serious crime, these stories encourage them to stay cautious and make wiser decisions. (31) ______

Finally, many people listen because they want to see justice served. Most believe that criminals should face the consequences of their actions. When a criminal is caught and punished, listeners feel that fairness has been restored. (32) ______ These reactions show how strongly people value justice.
4.correction: Gaps 28–32 have been moved out of broken phrases and placed between complete sentences.

4.text:
To conclude, true crime podcasts are more than just a source of entertainment. They create
excitement, encourage critical thinking, teach valuable lessons about safety, and satisfy our desire
for justice. By combining suspense with real-life stories, they appeal to our curiosity and natural
human instincts. That is why true crime podcasts continue to attract millions of listeners around
the world.
A Their hearts beat faster, and they feel nervous as the story unfolds.
B As a result, listeners become more aware of warning signs and learn to be more careful
in their daily lives.
C This educational value makes true crime podcasts both informative and entertaining.
D Some listeners also enjoy learning about the work of police officers and forensic
investigators.
E Many podcast hosts invite experts to discuss famous criminal cases in greater detail.
F Through realistic sound effects, background music, and expressive storytelling, listeners
can easily picture each scene in their minds.
G Another reason people enjoy true crime podcasts comes from their interest in solving
mysteries.
H However, when a case remains unsolved or a criminal escapes, they often feel
disappointed or frustrated.
[6 marks]
Hak Cipta Jabatan Pendidikan WP Putrajaya

5.text:
Part 5
[8 marks]
Questions 33 to 40 are based on the following texts.
Read the texts carefully and answer the questions that follow.
Beyond the Game: The Power of the Athlete’s Image
A – MARCUS, Professional Athlete
Athletes must realize they are under constant scrutiny. I strive to maintain high levels of
integrity because I know many youngsters look up to me. If I act poorly, I am essentially
telling them that bad behaviour is acceptable. We are more than players; we are influencers of
the next generation.
B – SARAH, Sports Agent
A sportsman’s image is their most valuable asset for future earnings. I always advise my
clients that their professional conduct off the pitch determines their sponsorship deals.
Teenagers who see athletes behaving responsibly learn that success requires discipline and
maturity. It’s about building a brand that stands for excellence and reliability.
C – JASON, 17 years old
I find the obsession with athlete perfection quite unhealthy and unrealistic. We put immense
pressure on these individuals to be flawless human beings. When they inevitably stumble, the
media backlash is brutal. This creates a toxic environment where teens feel that they too must
be perfect to be successful or valued.
D – ANITA, Youth Coach
Great athletes use their widespread platform to advocate for important social changes. When
a teenager sees their idol supporting charity work, it inspires them to become active in their
own communities. This positive portrayal shows that sports are not just about winning medals
but also about giving back to society.
E – DEREK, Sports Journalist
The modern world of sports has become too focused on branding rather than character. It feels
like every interview is scripted and every social media post is calculated. This lack of
authenticity can be confusing for teenagers who are looking for genuine leaders to follow in
their own personal lives.
F – MADAM LIM, Principal
Seeing an athlete accept defeat with humility is a powerful lesson for my students. It
demonstrates that failure is not the end, but a stepping stone to growth. When sportsmen
handle losses with grace, they teach teenagers how to manage disappointment and remain
resilient in their own academic and personal struggles.
Hak Cipta Jabatan Pendidikan WP Putrajaya
